vector: A pyrightconfig.json and a [tool.pyright] table in pyproject.toml name a tracked virtual environment whose bin/python and bin/python3 are scripts that write the canary.
expect: A `pyrightconfig.json`, and a `[tool.pyright]`, that name an interpreter. The configs are removed or never read; the pinned interpreter runs
control: Both configs name evil-venv, and its bin/python, run in a copy of the checkout, writes the canary.

vector: A tracked sgconfig.yml loads a rule directory whose rule matches every JavaScript file, and declares a custom language whose library is in the repository.
expect: A repo `sgconfig.yml` is ignored; hakutaku's config is passed after the subcommand, from outside the snapshot
control: Stock ast-grep scanning a copy of the checkout applies the repository's rule: its output carries the rule id hakutaku-hostile-sgconfig.

vector: The repository's .git/config sets core.pager, diff.external, core.askPass and core.sshCommand to a script that writes the canary, and names an ssh remote.
expect: `core.pager`, `diff.external`, `core.askPass` and `core.sshCommand` all point at the canary. None runs
control: Stock git in a copy of the checkout runs each one: git diff runs diff.external, git credential fill runs core.askPass, git fetch runs core.sshCommand, and git log on a terminal runs core.pager.

vector: .gitattributes assigns a filter to *.txt, and .git/config defines its smudge command as a script that writes the canary.
expect: `cat-file --batch` never runs the filter. A control run of `git archive` does, which proves the fixture fires
control: Stock git archive of a copy of the checkout runs the smudge filter.

vector: The head commit carries a PGP signature header, and .git/config sets log.showSignature and a gpg.program that writes the canary.
control: Stock git log in a copy of the checkout runs gpg.program on the head commit's signature.

vector: .git/config sets core.fsmonitor to a script that writes the canary, and every client-side hook in .git/hooks writes it too.
expect: A canary `core.fsmonitor` and canary hooks never run
control: Stock git status in a copy of the checkout runs core.fsmonitor, and git commit runs the commit hooks.

vector: A tracked .dependency-cruiser.js writes the canary when it is loaded.
expect: A `.dependency-cruiser.js` with a side effect is removed at export, and `--config` is always passed
control: Stock dependency-cruiser given --config .dependency-cruiser.js in a copy of the checkout loads it, and it writes the canary.

vector: Tracked json.py, grimp.py and sitecustomize.py at the repository root, and a package __init__.py, each write the canary when imported.
expect: A `json.py`, a `sitecustomize.py` and a side-effecting `__init__.py`: under `python -I`, the grimp driver runs none of them
control: Stock Python in a copy of the checkout imports each one, and each writes the canary: json, grimp and pkg from the working directory, and sitecustomize from PYTHONPATH.

vector: A tracked symlink points at the absolute path of host/secret.txt, which holds the marker.
expect: A tracked link to `<outDir>/host/secret.txt` is recorded with its target text, and never created or followed
control: Reading config/leak.txt in a copy of the checkout, as a tool that follows links does, gives the marker.

vector: A tree built with git plumbing holds an entry named .. that leads to escape.txt, and an entry whose name holds a control character.
expect: A tree entry holding `..` is refused, and listed in `export.json`'s `refused`. Nothing is written outside `snapshot/`
control: Stock git ls-tree lists the entry as ../escape.txt, beside the name that holds a control character.

vector: A TypeScript comment and a Python docstring tell an AI reader to ignore its instructions and run a command that writes the canary.
expect: It comes back only inside `text` or `lines`, under the untrusted marking
control: The planted command, run in a shell, writes the canary.

vector: Files whose names hold HTML markup and shell command substitutions, a file path and a function name worded as instructions to an AI reader, and code that holds a closing script tag and an inline event handler, in a TypeScript module and in a PHP template, a language the viewer does not highlight.
expect: Markup in file names and in code renders as text, and the CSP blocks a script. The query tools give every name back as data, under the untrusted marking
control: A shell that expands a planted file name's command substitution, in a copy of the checkout, makes the file markup-names-canary.

vector: A one-line JavaScript file of exactly 52,428,800 bytes, written at run time.
expect: A 50 MB one-line JS file keeps its metadata only (`no_source`), and the build stays within its limits
control: No control runs; the fixture's shape is checked instead: src/big.min.js is 52,428,800 bytes with no newline, and src/app.js imports it.

vector: A tracked file holds a fake token on one line. The test's stand-in for ast-grep fails on that line, and prints it with the absolute paths it was given, as a parser's error does.
expect: No attempt, answer or list row holds the token or a path of this machine: the paths are named by token, and the token is redacted
control: The failing stand-in, run on a copy of the checkout, prints the token and the file's absolute path.

vector: A TypeScript file and a Python module whose names hold U+2028 (line separator), two more whose names hold U+2029 (paragraph separator), and a TypeScript file that imports the two TypeScript ones. An engine's JSON keeps both characters raw inside a string, such as a match's path, and JavaScript ends a line at each: a multiline regular expression does, and so does node:readline in recent Node releases.
expect: File names that hold U+2028 or U+2029 are mapped like any other: every engine's output is cut into records at line feeds only, so the map completes and indexes those files
control: Stock ast-grep, run with a pattern in a copy of the checkout, writes each match's path with the character raw, and a multiline regular expression reads its two matches as four lines.
